mechanism_narrative: A rebound in parks visitation from the sharp t-2w trough to t-0w signals broader discretionary outing normalization, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks as the same households extend trips into shopping and dining corridors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks after a drop below -25
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps recovering but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average within 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When residential mobility remains above baseline while workplaces stay deeply negative, shopping shifts toward local and convenience retail rather than destination retail, producing a near-term rise in RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 while WORKPLACES stays below -20
failure_condition: If residential remains elevated and workplaces remain weak but RETAIL_REC falls or stays below its prior 4-week mean over the next 7-14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A steep fall in transit mobility below the recent range reduces access to high-street retail and suppresses shopping trips with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks after such a transit break.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 5 points week-on-week from an already sub -35 level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT makes a new weekly low and RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises over the next 14 days, the transit-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous upswing in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates more regular out-of-home routines and errand chaining, which spills over into retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both improve for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 28 days, this interaction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after the late-March slump captures warmer-weather outdoor activity, and that same seasonal lift extends to shopping and leisure trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive week-on-week after being below -20
evidence_refs: fact:parks rose from -38.7 at t-2w to -9.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If parks continue improving in spring but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines versus the last 28 days, the seasonal spillover claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains far below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, people substitute home-centered activity for discretionary shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to soften over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -35 for two straight weeks and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: If the TRANSIT-low/RESIDENTIAL-high pattern persists but RETAIL_REC rises within 14 days, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in WORKPLACES after a deep dip creates more weekday foot traffic and lunch-time spending, which lifts retail-and-recreation mobility over the next one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rebounds by at least 5 points from a trough below -25
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -28.6 at t-0w after earlier values near -15
failure_condition: If workplaces rebound but retail mobility remains below its prior 4-week mean through week 4, the commuting spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline while PARKS continues recovering, households are reallocating outings from necessity trips to discretionary trips, and RETAIL_REC should rise over the next week as the mix shifts toward shopping and leisure.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while GROCERY_PHARM stays within 2 points of its recent mean
failure_condition: If parks recover without any increase in RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days, despite stable grocery/pharmacy mobility, this reallocation hypothesis fails.
